helpText:
Every self-spot you send also goes to each channel listed here that is switched on.

**Webhook URL**: in Discord, open the channel's settings, then *Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook*, and copy its URL. Anyone holding that URL can post to the channel, so share it like a password.

**Message**: a template, written the way the app's other templates are. Besides `op` (the operation), it can name the spot itself:

- `spot.freq` — the frequency, in kHz
- `spot.mode` — the mode
- `spot.comments` — your spot comment
- `spot.qcode` — its Q-code, when it starts with one (`QRT`), always in capitals
- `spot.qrest` — the comment after that Q-code

These are the names Ham2K Portable Logger's Discord spotting uses, so a template from there keeps its `spot` values (its `spot.qCode` and `spot.qRest` work too) — written in this app's template syntax.

**Posted as** and **Avatar image URL** are templates too, for the name and picture the message appears under — `{{ op.station }}` posts as your callsign. Left empty, Discord shows the webhook's own.

The editor's preview shows the `spot` values blank; they are filled in when a spot is sent.

A new channel's message posts only the spots whose comment starts with QRV or QRT — `KI2D QRV till 1600 • US-1234 • 14285 SSB` — so the channel hears when you go on and off the air, not every respot. Edit it to change that: a message that comes out blank skips that channel, so a template can choose its spots: `{% if spot.qcode != 'QRT' %}…{% endif %}` posts every spot except the one saying you are going QRT.
noWebhooks: No Discord channel is switched on
urlRequired: Enter the webhook URL Discord gave you
notWebhook: This is not a Discord webhook URL
allSkipped: No Discord channel's message applies to this spot
